entities.summary: Giulio Alberoni was an Italian cardinal and statesman who played a crucial role in the politics of Philip V of Spain, serving as his Secretary of State from 1713 to 1726. Born in 1666, Alberoni's early life and education were marked by his connections to the Catholic Church and the Habsburg dynasty. He rose to prominence through his diplomatic and administrative skills, becoming a key figure in the War of the Spanish Succession and the Treaty of Utrecht. As a cardinal, Alberoni was appointed as the Archbishop of Valencia and later as the Cardinal-Dean of the College of Cardinals. His influence extended to the Italian Peninsula, where he worked to consolidate Habsburg power and promote Catholicism. Alberoni's legacy is complex, reflecting both his loyalty to the Habsburgs and his commitment to Italian interests. He died on June 26, 1752, at the age of 86, leaving behind a reputation as a skilled politician and diplomat. Despite his significant contributions to European politics, Alberoni's impact was largely overshadowed by the larger forces of the Enlightenment and the rise of liberal movements in Italy. Nevertheless, his career serves as a reminder of the enduring importance of the Catholic Church in shaping European politics and culture during the 18th century.
